title: Low-carbon cement binder chemistry
bottleneck: Cement production emits roughly 8 percent of global CO2, mostly from calcining limestone, and no alternative binder has matched Portland cement's strength, setting time, durability, and cost all at once. Alkali-activated and belite-rich cements cut emissions but suffer from variable feedstocks, efflorescence, or slow strength gain; carbon-cured concretes need CO2 supply chains that do not exist at scale. Standards written around Portland chemistry further block adoption.
why_it_blocks: Concrete is the most consumed material on Earth after water, and infrastructure demand keeps growing. Without a drop-in low-carbon binder, every new bridge and building locks in decades of process emissions that efficiency tweaks cannot erase.
current_state: Limestone-calcined-clay cements are cutting emissions 30-40 percent in commercial use, and several startups are piloting novel binders. But a true zero-process-emission binder proven over 50-year service life does not yet exist.
